speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS presenting with decreased vision and black spots in your right eye. Given your immunocompromised state, could you tell me if you experience any floaters, flashes of light, or curtain-like shadows over your vision?

REQUEST TEST: Ocular_Fundoscopy
REQUEST IMAGES: Fundus_Photo_Right_Eye

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text:
The findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages on funduscopy are highly concerning for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. Have you recently experienced any fever, night sweats, or significant weight loss?

REQUEST TEST: PCR for CMV from blood
REQUEST IMAGES: OCT_Right_Eye

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis. The combination of your profound immunosuppression (CD4 count of 36/mm³) and the characteristic retinal findings of granular opacities and hemorrhages confirms this diagnosis. We will initiate treatment with ganciclovir immediately.
